title: Specified compact-support source comparison for an equal factored chart
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$, $s:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$, $i:U\hookrightarrow P$ and $p:P\to V$ be morphisms of Noetherian schemes, with $s,v$ open, $i$ closed and a specified equality $fs=vpi$. Suppose every displayed morphism and its composites are separated of finite type and admit chosen compactifications. Work in the ordinary unbounded etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Let $n_s,n_v,n_i$ be the specified bounded-below immersion normalizations [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization] and let $\alpha_{b,a}:Rb_!Ra_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(ba)_!$ be the canonical bounded-below compositors [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. There is a natural isomorphism, evaluated in the ambient unbounded category only on $H\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $$\gamma_H:Rf_!Ds_!H\xrightarrow{\sim}Dv_!Rp_!Di_*H.$$ Its specified value is $$\gamma_H=n_{v,Rp_!Di_*H}\circ Rv_!Rp_!(n_{i,H})\circ Rv_!(\alpha_{p,i,H}^{-1})\circ\alpha_{v,pi,H}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{f,s,H}\circ Rf_!(n_{s,H}^{-1}),$$ with transport along $fs=vpi$ between the middle compact-support values. All normalizations and compositors in this formula are evaluated on bounded-below inputs, and all intermediate values lie in $D^+$. The isomorphism is compatible with the canonical changes of compactification and, for every $a:H'\to H$ between bounded-below objects, satisfies $$\gamma_H\circ(Rf_!Ds_!)(a)=(Dv_!Rp_!Di_*)(a)\circ\gamma_{H'}.$$ In particular this specifies the normalized chart comparison as an actual natural transformation, rather than merely asserting that its source and target are isomorphic. No right adjoints or Hom comparison are asserted.

proof.text: First check the domains in the ambient unbounded category. For any chosen compactification $q=rj$ occurring here and $K$ with $\mathcal H^a(K)=0$ for $a<m$, the module-sheaf categories have enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] on the source to represent $K$ by an injective complex $I$ zero in degrees below $m$. By [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $Dj_!K$ is represented by the degreewise complex $j_!I$, also zero below $m$. Apply the same representative lemma on the compactification to obtain an injective complex $J$, zero below $m$, representing $Dj_!K$. It is K-injective by part (2) of that lemma. The computation of total direct image in [def-amb-etale-compact-support], applied to the identity resolution of $J$, gives $Rq_!K\cong Q(r_*J)$. This complex is zero below $m$, since degreewise extension by zero and direct image carry the zero module sheaf to zero. Thus every compact-support candidate used below preserves $D^{\ge m}$ and hence $D^+$. This argument applies to the already chosen compactifications; it needs no cohomological-dimension bound.

source.place: Tag 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist), parts (2)-(3), and Tag 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), applied to the candidate of more-etale.tex preceding Tag 0F7I; enough injectives: injectives.tex Tag 01DU.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization], $Ds_!H$ and $Di_*H$ are bounded below whenever $H$ is, and so is $Dv_!L$ for bounded-below $L$. Step 1 now places $Rp_!Di_*H$ and every iterated compact-support value below in $D^+$. All applications of the compositors in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] are legitimate: $(f,s)$, $(v,pi)$ and $(p,i)$ consist of compactifiable separated finite-type maps of Noetherian schemes, including the indicated composite $pi$, by the hypotheses. Start with the following three isomorphisms, in the displayed order: $$Rf_!Ds_!H\xrightarrow{Rf_!(n_{s,H}^{-1})}Rf_!Rs_!H\xrightarrow{\alpha_{f,s,H}}R(fs)_!H\xrightarrow{\alpha_{v,pi,H}^{-1}}Rv_!R(pi)_!H.$$ In the last arrow first transport $R(fs)_!H$ to $R(vpi)_!H$ along the specified equality $fs=vpi$. This transport is substitution along equality, so is natural in $H$; one may eliminate that equality to check this with identical functors.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), with Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined); normalized factored-chart specialization.

proof.text: Continue the preceding chain by $$Rv_!R(pi)_!H\xrightarrow{Rv_!(\alpha_{p,i,H}^{-1})}Rv_!Rp_!Ri_!H\xrightarrow{Rv_!Rp_!(n_{i,H})}Rv_!Rp_!Di_*H\xrightarrow{n_{v,Rp_!Di_*H}}Dv_!Rp_!Di_*H.$$ The first arrow is the inverse of the $(p,i)$ compositor of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], whiskered by $Rv_!$. The second and third arrows use exactly the closed normalization $n_i:Ri_!\to Di_*$ and the open normalization $n_v:Rv_!\to Dv_!$ of [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization]. In particular $n_v$ is evaluated at $Rp_!Di_*H$, which is bounded below by steps 1 and 2. Compose these three arrows with those of step 2 and call the resulting morphism $\gamma_H$. Reading the arrows from right to left as a product gives exactly the six-factor formula in the statement, with the specified equality transport.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), with Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined); normalized factored-chart specialization.

proof.text: Each arrow in steps 2 and 3 is an isomorphism. For a functor $F$ and an isomorphism $u$, $F(u^{-1})F(u)=F(u^{-1}u)=1$ and likewise in the other order. Thus whiskering preserves each inverse. Reversing the six arrows (and the equality transport) and taking their inverses gives an inverse to $\gamma_H$: adjacent pairs cancel by associativity. This proves invertibility with the specified component formula.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), with Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined); normalized factored-chart specialization.

proof.text: Let $F_0,\ldots,F_6$ be the successive functors in the six-arrow chain of steps 2 and 3, with the equality transport included in the third arrow, and let $t_j:F_{j-1}\to F_j$ be its arrows. For $a:H^\prime\to H$ in $D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, naturality of the normalizations in [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization] and of the compositors in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] gives $$t_{j,H}F_{j-1}(a)=F_j(a)t_{j,H^\prime}.$$ This also holds for inverses by multiplying the original naturality equation by the two inverse components, and for whiskered arrows by applying the outer functor; for $n_v$ apply its naturality to $(Rp_!Di_*)(a)$. Substituting these six equalities successively in $t_{6,H}\cdots t_{1,H}F_0(a)$ gives $$\gamma_HF_0(a)=F_6(a)\gamma_{H^\prime}.$$ Consequently the constructed components define an actual natural transformation on $D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ with values in $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Together with step 4 this is the required natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), with Tag 0F7I (lemma-shriek-well-defined); normalized factored-chart specialization.

proof.text: Finally change any chosen compactifications. Denote the old and new chain functors by $F_j,F_j^\prime$ and their arrows by $t_j,t_j^\prime$. The canonical comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], whiskered through the successive factors, give $c_j:F_j\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j^\prime$; the exact functors $Ds_!,Di_*,Dv_!$ themselves stay fixed. Independence of the compositors from compactification choices gives the comparison squares for the compositor arrows. Compatibility of the specified normalizations with compactification changes in [lem-sf-etale-immersion-shriek-normalization] gives those squares for the normalization arrows. For an inverse arrow multiply its comparison square by inverses; for an outer functor that also changes, first use the naturality of its comparison at the inner arrow and then the inner comparison square. These operations give, for each $j$, $$c_jt_j=t_j^\prime c_{j-1}.$$ Equality transport is compatible with these equations by eliminating $fs=vpi$. Multiply the six equations and cancel the intermediate comparisons to obtain $$c_6\gamma=\gamma^\prime c_0.$$ Here $c_0$ is the change of $Rf_!Ds_!$, and $c_6$ is $Dv_!$ applied to the change of $Rp_!$ at $Di_*$. This is precisely compatibility with canonical changes of compactification. The identity and cocycle laws already stated in [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] make this valid for successive changes as well.
